findings.title: Floating-point multiplication before rounding
findings.body: `totalCents(booking) * (percent / 100)` performs floating-point arithmetic, which can introduce tiny rounding errors before `Math.round` is applied. This can cause the final cents to be off by one when the share is very close to a rounding boundary. Use integer arithmetic or a fixed-point library to avoid this.

findings.title: Unnecessary rounding before conversion to cents
findings.body: `Math.round(share)` is applied to a floating-point value, then `toCents` is called. If `toCents` already rounds or truncates, this double rounding is redundant and may cause the result to differ from expectations. Remove the rounding step and let `toCents` handle the conversion.

summary.problem: The new `depositCents` function uses floating-point arithmetic and redundant rounding, risking off-by-one errors in cents.
summary.done_well: The function clearly separates the calculation of the share and its conversion to cents, and it reuses existing utilities (`totalCents`, `toCents`).
